user_class: AI-native filmmakers producing multi-scene narrative shorts
painful_workflow: They manually re-prompt for every new shot, struggling to maintain consistent character appearance, lighting, and world details across scenes. They waste significant hackathon time on trial-and-error prompt tweaking instead of directing the story.
unmet_need: A way to automatically propagate a defined visual bible (character portraits, environment look, color palette) into every scene's generation prompt so that stylistic and identity consistency is guaranteed without manually copying descriptors.
why_now: The hackathon's judging criteria heavily weights storytelling (35%) and visual consistency under technical capability, while fal's Assets system is purpose-built for reusable character identity but remains underutilized without automated prompt-chain tooling.
unresolved_claims: Whether fal Assets already supports automated injection into multi-model pipelines via the Workflows API
If hackathon participants actually recognize style drift as their primary failure mode versus other time sinks

user_class: Developer-track participants building AI-video tools under extreme time pressure
painful_workflow: They must demonstrate a polished, working tool in a 3-minute demo video, but any real-time AI generation failure or latency spike during the demo recording can ruin the presentation. They lack guardrails to handle model errors gracefully under a 72-hour constraint.
unmet_need: A lightweight development pattern or library that automatically catches real-time generation failures and falls back to pre-computed or lower-fidelity alternative outputs, ensuring a demo never freezes or shows raw error states.
why_now: The hackathon's Developer Track weights demo impressiveness at 15% but technical execution at 35%; a single visible glitch can destroy both. The 'potentially_underexplored' analysis explicitly calls out demo-failure surface minimization as a high-value gap.
unresolved_claims: Whether the fal API's error codes are predictable enough to build reliable fallback logic within the hackathon window
If judges interpret pre-rendered fallback segments as a lack of real-time boldness rather than engineering maturity

user_class: Small brand and advertising creative teams producing short-form AI commercials
painful_workflow: They iterate through dozens of AI-generated video drafts to find one that matches brand guidelines, but have no systematic way to compare versions side-by-side on specific brand attributes (logo visibility, color accuracy, tone). Evaluation is purely subjective and slows decision-making.
unmet_need: A structured review interface that overlays brand guideline checks (color palette match percentage, logo presence detection, tone classifier) onto generated video candidates, enabling objective side-by-side comparison.
why_now: The Generative Media Track includes dedicated Brand & Advertising theme, and the resource guide warns against incremental wrappers, but no current tool addresses the brand-compliance feedback loop—a clear gap for a Developer Track submission that brings measurable user value to Gen Media creators.
unresolved_claims: Whether automated brand compliance checks would be perceived as creatively constraining by hackathon judges focused on originality (30% of GenMedia score)
If logo/color detection models can run reliably within fal's serverless infrastructure during a live hack

user_class: Solo generative media artists creating anime-style short films
painful_workflow: They want to produce high-quality anime with unique, personal art styles, but the default model outputs look generic. To achieve a distinctive aesthetic, they must manually post-process frames or write extremely complex single-prompt style descriptions that still drift.
unmet_need: A way to fine-tune or condition the generation pipeline on a custom style reference pack (character sheets, key background art, color scripts) so that every generated frame conforms to a unique, non-generic anime aesthetic without manual per-frame correction.
why_now: Anime is an explicit Generative Media Track theme, and 'generic anime characters' is flagged as a high-collision risk. The hackathon offers Grok Imagine and Kling via fal API, which could be orchestrated with style-reference injection to escape the generic look—aligning with the 'multi-model synergy beyond chaining' underexplored area.
unresolved_claims: Whether Grok Imagine or Kling support style-reference conditioning through the fal API at the time of the hackathon
If hackathon participants will consider 'custom style conditioning' a developer tool or a generative media asset pipeline worthy of a Developer Track entry
